headline: A law that extends federal programs for preserving sound recordings and films through 2026 and changes the size and makeup of one foundation's board.
what_it_does: It extends the Library of Congress's national sound recording preservation program and the National Recording Preservation Foundation through fiscal year 2026, with funding capped at the lesser of $1 million or the private contributions the Foundation receives. It increases the Foundation's board from 9 to 12 members and requires at least 8 of them to have knowledge or experience in sound recording work. It also extends the National Film Registry and the National Film Preservation Foundation through fiscal year 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Library of Congress and its sound recording preservation program
who_it_affects.how: The program's authorization is extended through fiscal year 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the National Recording Preservation Foundation's board of directors
who_it_affects.how: The board grows from 9 seats to 12, with at least 8 members needing sound recording experience.

who_it_affects.group: Private donors and state and local governments that contribute to the National Recording Preservation Foundation
who_it_affects.how: Their contributions set the ceiling on federal funding, which is the lesser of $1 million or the amount they give.

who_it_affects.group: Film archivists and the National Film Preservation Foundation
who_it_affects.how: The National Film Registry and the Foundation are reauthorized through fiscal year 2026.

when_it_takes_effect: The reauthorizations run through fiscal year 2026; the bill summary does not give a specific start date.
